notes:
Summary: Lighthouse Archive Search indexing legacy legal documents + client contracts (~120M docs). Primary focus: replace current embeddings store and introduce learned reranker to improve precision@k while keeping median retrieval latency <120ms at 95thpct. Cost sensitivity: strict constraint on cost-per-query (target < $0.06/query with batching + cache).

Key technical constraints / asks:
- Index size: ~120M docs; average doc vector 1536 dims, many short docs (clauses) -> expect heavy index IO and storage.
- Latency targets: 50ms median retrieval, 95th pct < 120ms for simple retrieval; rerank step budgeted ~60-120ms depending on model; end-to-end RAG latency target < 300ms for support workflows.
- Migration plan: offline evals comparing current embeddings (in-house SBERT variant) vs candidate open/embed models; reranker A/B between LightRerank v1 (current) and proposed cross-encoder. Evals include automatic metrics (nDCG, MRR, precision@1/5) + human side-by-side relevance judgments (legal SME panel).
- Rollout requirements: canary by customer segment, AB testing with traffic steering, automatic rollback on quality regression (eval-driven). Need Redwood support for canary/A-B + model variant routing + metric hooks to Redwood Console.
- Security: must keep EU-residency for raw documents; SSO/SAML + audit logs + KMS integration required. On-prem option for archive-sensitive clients.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We cannot accept any model change that increases Type I errors on precedence docs — legal risk is real." — Head of Product.
- "We want a baseline run against our 5M working-set, offline evals first, then a 10% canary controlling for client type." — CTO.

POC success criteria (short):
- Embedding quality: +6–10% relative uplift in nDCG@10 vs current baseline on labeled eval set (500 queries).
- Reranker: at least parity in accuracy on precedence-sensitive queries, with latency <120ms at 95thpct on Dedicated nodes.
- Cost: projected cost-per-query < $0.06 at expected 10k qps/day using batching + prefix caching.

Notes on operations/observability asked for:
- Token-level cost breakdown in Console for canary vs baseline routes.
- Per-prompt latency breakdown and tracing hooks for reranker failures.
- Eval-driven regression alerts tied to nightly evals and human review pipelines.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Exact Dedicated node sizing recommendations for 120M docs + expected qps (want cost estimate and perf curves).
- How Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles for cross-encoder rerankers without degrading legal-critical relevance.
- Can Redwood host audit logs in EU region and integrate with our KMS?

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to provide Dedicated sizing + cost estimate (by 2026-03-15).
- SE to provision POC sandbox for 5M subset and run baseline embedding + reranker sweep.
- Security team to schedule compliance call (SAML/KMS) week of 2026-03-15.

- Strong buying signal: legal/regulatory drivers force lower tolerance for regressions, willing to pay premium for auditable rollouts.
